sources.label: Wikipedia pageviews (editions: en es hi zh id ur pt bn ru am ha yo)
sources.terms_quote: All Analytics datasets are available under the Creative Commons CC0 dedication. Bots must "Accurately identify your User-Agent" and honor Retry-After (https://wikitech.wikimedia.org/wiki/Robot_policy).
sources.decision: Used: REST API top lists and per-article series, identifying User-Agent, one request per 0.25 s.

sources.label: Wikimedia pageviews per country (differentially private)
sources.terms_quote: Release threshold: For lower risk, 90 pageviews. For medium risk, 550 pageviews. For higher risk, 1000 pageviews. License: "All Analytics datasets are available under the Creative Commons CC0 dedication" (https://dumps.wikimedia.org/other/analytics/); the dataset's own README states no separate licence.
sources.decision: Used for countries with enough published rows. Counts are noisy by design (median relative error <= 6-8%) and only pages above the release threshold appear: days below it count as the threshold, never as 0. No data is published for China and Russia.
sources.unit: pageviews/day (first 10 unique per device, differentially private)

sources.label: Wikidata (topics, classes, dated events)
sources.terms_quote: Wikidata requires a CC0 license, which is equivalent to public domain.
sources.decision: Used: Action API (search, entities) and the Query Service with an identifying User-Agent.

sources.label: GDELT 15-minute GKG files (news)
sources.license: free use, cite the GDELT Project
sources.terms_quote: all datasets released by the GDELT Project are available for unlimited and unrestricted use for any academic, commercial, or governmental use of any kind without fee. Any use or redistribution must include a citation to the GDELT Project and a link to this website (https://www.gdeltproject.org/).
sources.decision: Used: data.gdeltproject.org files only (not the rate-limited DOC API). Country = articles mentioning a place in that country.

sources.label: Hacker News
sources.license: Hacker News API terms (title, link, points only)
sources.terms_quote: This API is built on top of Algolia Search's API. It enables developers to access HN data programmatically.
sources.decision: Used for Worldwide only (no country concept); title, link and points are kept.

sources.label: YouTube mostPopular chart (by region)
sources.terms_quote: an API Client must not store statistics retrieved as Non-Authorized Data for more than 30 days. Your API Clients must not (i) replace API Data with similar, independently calculated data, or (ii) access or use API Data to create new or derived data or metrics.
sources.decision: Used with the key from the operator's secrets file (YOUTUBE_API_KEY, never printed). Chart presence and the raw viewCount are shown as YouTube reports them; they feed no ratio and no score strength. Refreshed on every daily build; the build keeps nothing between runs (do not commit dated copies of the youtube channel to git history: the policy limits storing non-authorized statistics to 30 days). 1 quota unit per region per day, nicheclock budget 3,000 of 10,000 units.

sources.label: Public holidays (holidays package)
sources.terms_quote: Copyright (c) Vacanza Team and individual contributors (MIT licence, github.com/vacanza/holidays/blob/dev/LICENSE).
sources.decision: Used for the 10 countries; dates are facts.

sources.label: Federal Register
sources.license: US government work, public domain (17 U.S.C. 105)
sources.terms_quote: Due to aggressive automated scraping of FederalRegister.gov and eCFR.gov, programmatic access to these sites is limited to access to our extensive developer APIs.
sources.decision: Used through the documented API; US only.

sources.label: Nager.Date holidays
sources.license: private or non-profit use; commercial needs sponsorship
sources.terms_quote: The Web API can be used for private or non-profit projects. For commercial purposes we require active sponsorship. It is not allowed to use the holiday information to publish or operate your own holiday portal.
sources.decision: Excluded: nicheclock is public with planned pricing. The MIT holidays package covers the same 10 countries.

sources.label: Apple Marketing Tools RSS (top apps, podcasts, music by country)
sources.terms_quote: The RSS Generator is listed under "Advanced Tools" of the Apple Services Performance Partner Program: "Use the RSS Feed Generator to incorporate lists for top music, apps, books, and more. You can add these feeds to your website or view them using a standard RSS feed reader."
sources.decision: Excluded until someone confirms the feed terms: it is a tool of the affiliate programme and no public statement allows redistributing chart data in a product. Easy to enable once confirmed.

sources.label: TMDB
sources.terms_quote: Its licence requires a commercial agreement.
sources.decision: Not used: its licence requires a commercial agreement.

sources.label: Spotify charts
sources.terms_quote: Its terms do not allow reuse of chart data.
sources.decision: Not used: its terms do not allow reuse of chart data.

sources.label: Google Play
sources.terms_quote: It has no API and its terms forbid scraping.
sources.decision: Not used: it has no API and its terms forbid scraping.

sources.label: Google Trends internal RPC
sources.terms_quote: Its terms do not allow automated use of that endpoint.
sources.decision: Not used: its terms do not allow automated use of that endpoint.

sources.label: Baidu
sources.terms_quote: Its terms do not clearly allow this use.
sources.decision: Not used: its terms do not clearly allow this use.

sources.label: Weibo
sources.terms_quote: Its terms do not clearly allow this use.
sources.decision: Not used: its terms do not clearly allow this use.

sources.label: ReliefWeb
sources.decision: Milestone 2: terms to be read and quoted before the source is switched on.

sources.label: Mastodon trending tags
sources.decision: Milestone 2: terms to be read and quoted before the source is switched on.

sources.label: Bluesky
sources.decision: Milestone 2: terms to be read and quoted before the source is switched on.

sources.label: GH Archive (hourly stars and forks of public repos)
sources.terms_quote: GH Archive is a project to record the public GitHub timeline, archive it, and make it easily accessible for further analysis. ... Note this repository does not contain the GH Archive dataset (event archives/data). The dataset includes material that may be subject to third party rights. (robots.txt: no Disallow; Cloudflare content-signal comment only)
sources.decision: Experimental, off by default: the catalog build skips this source unless it is named in --experimental. Read its terms before switching it on. When on, it is used with care: the hourly files are streamed and reduced to repo name -> stars and forks per day (WatchEvent/ForkEvent). No actor names, payloads or text are stored or published. The licence of the dataset is not stated, so only counts of public events (facts) leave the build. Re-read the terms before enabling it.

sources.label: GitHub REST API (repo description, language, topics, totals)
sources.terms_quote: You may not use the API to download data or Content from GitHub for spamming purposes, including for the purposes of selling GitHub users' personal information, such as to recruiters, headhunters, and job boards. (GitHub Terms of Service, API Terms)
sources.decision: Used read-only with the operator's token (never printed) for public repository metadata only (name, description, language, topics, star/fork totals). The github.com/trending page itself is not fetched for the product (GitHub AUP).

sources.label: GDACS current disaster events
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 (European Commission reuse policy), source acknowledged
sources.terms_quote: GDACS is a cooperation framework among United Nations (OCHA and UNOSAT) and the European Commission (JRC and ECHO) ... While we try everything to ensure accuracy, this information is purely indicative and should not be used for any decision making without alternate sources of information. (GDACS terms of use). The Commission's reuse policy is implemented by the Commission Decision of 12 December 2011 on the reuse of Commission documents ... under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) licence. (https://commission.europa.eu/legal-notice_en)
sources.decision: Used: the public events list (one request a day), event name, type, alert level, country, date and link. Shown as present events with GDACS's own alert level, 'indicative only' as GDACS says; no score of ours. Source credited in every row.

sources.label: TVmaze schedules
sources.terms_quote: Licensing: Use of the TVmaze API is licensed by CC BY-SA. ... You can satisfy the attribution requirement by linking back to TVmaze from within your application or website, for example using the URLs available in the API. ... it's useful to gracefully handle HTTP 429 responses.
sources.decision: Used: shows with an episode airing today per country (11 requests a day), name, type, language, network, TVmaze's own popularity weight and the show link as attribution. No descriptions or images are copied.

sources.label: Stack Overflow hot questions (tags)
sources.license: Stack Exchange API; content CC BY-SA, not copied
sources.terms_quote: (c) Stack Exchange, Inc; user contributions licensed under CC BY-SA (footer of https://api.stackexchange.com/docs). Quota: by default 10,000 requests a day for an application with a key, far fewer without one (https://api.stackexchange.com/docs/throttle). The Terms of Use page itself answered 403 to a script, so it was not read.
sources.decision: Experimental, off by default: the catalog build skips this source unless it is named in --experimental. Read its terms before switching it on. When on, it is used with care: one request a day for the 100 hottest questions; only the tag names, their counts and a link to the tag page are kept, never question text. Re-read the terms before enabling it (the API Terms of Use were not readable by script).

sources.label: PyPI download counts (pypistats.org)
sources.license: download counts as published; names and counts only
sources.terms_quote: PyPI Stats provides a simple JSON API for retrieving aggregate download stats and time series for packages. ... All download data is updated once daily. Etiquette: If you plan on using the API to download historical data for every python package in the database, DON'T. This website runs on limited resources. IP-based rate limiting is imposed application-wide.
sources.decision: Experimental, off by default: the catalog build skips this source unless it is named in --experimental. Read its terms before switching it on. When on, it is used with care: the 60 most downloaded packages (hugovk/top-pypi-packages list, so nobody hand-picks packages), one request each per day, 1 s apart, nothing historical beyond the 28-day series the endpoint returns. No licence statement was found for the counts: only package names, counts and a link are kept. Re-read the terms before enabling it.

sources.label: Open Library daily trending
sources.license: Open Library API terms (light use, identifying User-Agent)
sources.terms_quote: These APIs are not intended to serve as a bulk data backend or high-traffic commercial infrastructure. For bulk access, please download our free monthly data dumps ... If you are doing high-volume calls, please add a HEADER that specifies a User-Agent string with (a) the name of your application and (b) your contact email.
sources.decision: Used: one request a day for the daily trending works, title, authors and link only; the shared client sends the identifying User-Agent.
sources.unit: rank on the daily trending list

sources.label: CoinGecko (free demo API)
sources.license: no commercial rights on the free plan
sources.terms_quote: Does the Demo (free) API plan include commercial rights? No, to use CoinGecko API data commercially, you'll need to upgrade to a paid plan. Attribution alone does not grant commercial rights on the Demo plan. ... Yes [the keyless API can be used in a commercial product], but you still need an active paid API plan.
sources.decision: Excluded: nicheclock is a public product with planned pricing, and the free plan has no commercial rights. Can be enabled with a paid plan (attribution 'Data powered by CoinGecko'); Finance is already above 10 rows without it.

sources.label: npm download counts
sources.license: no reuse statement; no official top list
sources.terms_quote: There is a public api that gives you download counts by package and time range. (npm registry docs). The docs state no licence for reuse, and there is no official list of the most downloaded packages.
sources.decision: Excluded for now: without an objective top list the packages would have to be chosen by hand, which the catalog does not do. PyPI covers the same need with a published top list.
